question.text: An AIF set up in GIFT-City IFSC intends to register as an FPI under SEBI (Foreign Portfolio Investors) Regulations, 2019 to invest in Indian listed securities. Under the FPI Regulations, what is the mandatory Sponsor commitment for a Cat III AIF-FPI?

answer.text: 2.5% of corpus or USD 750,000, whichever is lower
5% of corpus or USD 1.5 million, whichever is lower
INR 10 crore flat, as per domestic Cat III rule

explanation.text: The Logic: For AIFs set up in IFSC and registering as FPIs, the mandatory Sponsor commitment for a Cat III AIF-FPI is 5% of corpus or USD 1.5 million, whichever is lower. The Cat I/II equivalent under the same regime is 2.5% of corpus or USD 7,50,000, whichever is lower. The Manager/Sponsor in this set-up is required to be a person resident in India for FEMA purposes. The Trap: Option A states the Cat I/II rule (2.5% / USD 7,50,000) rather than the Cat III rule. Option B uses a 10% percentage with no cap, which is not the regulatory commitment. Option D imports the domestic INR-denominated Cat III rule rather than the IFSC AIF-FPI calibration. Note: Lock in the two paired thresholds: Cat I/II IFSC AIF-FPI at 2.5% or USD 7,50,000 (lower) and Cat III at 5% or USD 1.5 million (lower); both use the "whichever is lower" cap.
